text: This is a worse version of Panera. Panera sucks. Honestly, that's probably all you really need to know right there, but I will of course elaborate... We had seen this place pop up and were somewhat excited to give them a try. Wound up in the area randomly and were hungry for breakfast, but wanted it on the go. Kneaders has a drive-thru so we figured it was worth a try. I went with the reuben panini, and my wife got the harvest vegetable sandwich. We both got chocolate croissants and I got a large iced tea, she had a coffee with cream. The best items were the croissants. Not the best I've ever had but they were nice. They were light and crispy on the outside, the chocolate had a nice flavor. In descending order, I think my wife's sandwich was the second best item, but it was a little odd. The roasted vegetables were good, and the bread was good, but there was a cheese on it that you would think and expect to be cream cheese that turns out to be ricotta. And its not like super high-grade ricotta either. It made the sandwich weird. From there, the food is a drastic drop off in flavor and quality. My reuben was thin, soggy, and one of the worst sandwiches I've had in a long time. I thought this was supposed to be a panini...You know, like crispy on the outside? No. It was complete mushy awfulness. Both of our sandwiches came with potato chips that were not cooked all the way through, so they were crispy on the outside and soft once you bit into them. Terrible. My wife's coffee was clearly burnt and my iced tea had no ice. The only vaguely redeeming factor to this place was that the people working there were very nice. And the croissants were good. Apart from that, everything was just awful. This is not a chain that is going to survive in Tucson, I'd like to think we have higher standards.

text: Copeland's has been a favorite of mine for years and I would visit the one in Kenner every time I'm in town. I grew up in Kenner/Metairie and visit 2-3 times per year. I looked forward to my Copeland's meal more than any others. Sadly, the Kenner location has been going downhill. The past few times I've been there, the service, and even worse, the way the manager ignores issues, has not been good. To make a long story short, there were 5 negatives during one last visit that finally convinced me not to go back, all of which would have been forgiven and forgotten if the manager would have had any semblance of caring, and would not have been so rude and dismissive. I'll spare you the verbose details, but here's the gist of it... -- First, this might sound trivial to some, but the plastic menus were so sticky they stuck to our fingers (so much that mine made noise every time I peeled my fingers off of it) -- not very appetizing as you peruse the delicious food offerings. -- A very simple request of "no onions" on a hickory sauce burger turned into a situation where the burger was eventually eaten ice cold, with a cold side of hickory sauce, after everyone else had finished their meals. With no apologies from anyone at any point. (The onions had mixed in with the sauce and cheese, so we couldn't brush them off easily.) -- The original food order took 45 minutes to arrive (and was barely warm), the failed attempt at correcting the burger issue took three steps and another 15-20 minutes. -- A to-go order placed plenty early was forgotten and didn't arrive until 20 minutes after we paid the bill. -- The chef was wandering around the restaurant and then sitting comfortably in the bar involved in a lengthy conversation with the bartender, while customers were waiting to order drinks and food orders were being botched. -- The manager eventually stopped by the table (of his own accord) and asked if there was a problem, but when we chose to nicely share the situation, he offered an insincere apology and walked away uninterested, not even offering to remind the staff to be more attentive or offering a complimentary dessert or drink (not that we wanted it, but a gesture goes a long way). Keep in mind that I've loved Copeland's for years. I'm sad that this location has been slipping, and now it's off my list. I hope the problems are addressed, because I will miss it. Clean your sticky menus off, for a start.

It's a cold day out and I ordered delivery and they deliver via bicycle. I'm sure if I ordered in the store, it would have been perfect. text: When the limited selection of cheap-looking (over-priced) lamps and light fixtures at The Home Depot and Lowe's just won't cut it, perhaps you should stop by Hermitage Lighting Gallery. This is a true lighting store with a full range of lighting solutions to please most tastes, I believe. Hermitage Lighting Gallery also offers (or can order) all manner of switches and bulbs, as well asother home hardware and accessories. The staff are not always sunny, but they are not snooty and ultimately helpful. The irony is that the overall lighting in the place is rather dim, in spite of all the fixtures and lamps in use. Walking around the store, I have seen a few lamps that look sharp and feel like quality products, but with price-tags in excess of $300, I admire and move on. Some of the fixtures are double or triple the price of somewhat similar fixtures at The Home Depot, for example, but the difference in price is truly analogous to the difference in quality. As the son of an electrician, I've seen a light fixture or two and I'm not sure that anything at Hermitage Lighting Gallery is cheap garbage, such as you find at the big box stores. I did find some "semi-flush" dome fixtures by Kichler that were around $31 each and I got two for my house. No, they are not high-end, but again, they are obviously better quality than (in this case) comparably-priced fixtures at The Home Depot. I paid close to $150, I believe, for my living-room fixture, but it's worth it. Again, the quality of design and construction is evident as it is, but more apparent when compared to a cheap-looking and poorly-made $59 version at The Home Depot. If you want to be inspired to update your home - and you're willing to pay a little more - go to Hermitage Lighting Gallery.
label: POS

text: I have nothing but great things to say about this restaurant. My husband and I dropped in one Sunday for an early, light dinner and ended up leaving completely stuffed. We only intended to order a drink and grab an appetizer or two, but we ended up with four appetizers because we couldn't decide. All of them were EXCELLENT. The assorted breads with infused butters were unbelievable. It came fresh and hot with soft pretzel bread, croissant roll, a spicy cornbread of sorts and a bread that looked and tasted like carrot cake. They served it with an apple butter and a chive/onion type butter, and the combinations were absolutely perfect! The meatball dish was much larger than we anticipated. It was packed full of cheddar grits, meatballs and mushrooms. This dish was delicious, though the giant mushrooms grossed my husband out a bit - I loved them! The ale and smoked cheddar dip served with the house made pretzel bread was incredibly rich and tasty - rich enough that you would definitely want to share it with one or two others. The beer braised onions absolutely made this dish. Finally, the garlic herbed fries. There were ridiculously good, and I highly recommend that you ask for a side of the buttermilk ranch to dip them in. I really didn't think this restaurant could go above and beyond even with their fries, but they did! I can't even describe it - you'll have to just try it for yourself! We wanted so badly to get dessert, but we just couldn't after all of that bread and carb loading. Needless to say, we will be back to do so!

The service was perfect and the waitress was extremely friendly and efficient. She kept our water glasses full, which is quite an accomplishment because we drink probably 5-7 glasses with our meals. On the recommendation of the waitress I ordered the surf and turf, mainly due to her boast that the steak was aged and so tender it could be cut with a fork. After we ordered, we were brought a selection of breads that were AMAZING! It was extremely difficult not to ruin our meal by gorging on bread. My two favorites were the jalapeño cheddar and the pumpkin spice. When our entrees arrived I discovered that the steak was indeed so tender that it did not require a knife. The reduction on top was very flavorful and the crawfish added just the right amount of kick. The fish was cooked so well that even the "fish haters" in our group loved the flavor. All employees were smiling and seemed to genuinely be enjoying themselves. The Crispy Oysters were served as five on top of the oyster shells. Each oyster was crispy fried and topped with a creamy glaze. They were extremely crispy on the outside, moist and delicious on the inside. The quality was excellent. The Truffle Macaroni and Cheese was served in a small boat with shaved black truffle and rich, creamy cheese. The top was slightly browned to add a slightly crispy texture. The quality was excellent. The Brussel Sprouts were served in a small boat and halved. They were garnished with small onion slices, bacon pieces, and caramelized for a crisp bite. They were slightly undersalted, however the bacon made up for this. They tasted fresh and were very good. The Swordfish was served hot on a hot plate. A warm crab salad sat on top of the fish, which was also topped with avocado. The swordfish had a steak-like quality, though was still flaky and moist throughout. The flavor was excellent and was perfectly seasoned. This exceeded my expectations. The Lemon Sole was served hot on a warm plate. The fish, although thin, was long and met my expectations. The flavor and quality were excellent. The Bananas Foster Cake was served on a hot plate and lit aflame by the server who delivered it. The butter pecan iced cream had not yet melted and had a rich buttery flavor that paired extremely well with the banana buttercake. text: After a jaunt to NOMA on a Friday night, we decided to get a late dinner at Santa Fe. The menu was Mexican inspired, very creative, and well loved by food aficionados such as myself. The space too was beautiful and charming. In fact it was here that I was introduced to the straight up martini, much to my delight and ultimate chagrin. I always loved my evenings here. So it was with much sadness that the place did not re-open after the Storm. The restaurant was sold and re-opened on Esplanade in the space previously occupied by Greg Sonnier's Gabrielle, another favorite also shuttered by the Storm. I had been to the new Santa Fe only once and, for some reason, thought it to be simply a Tex Mex kind of place. I was totally wrong as I found out during my recent visit. Although the menu does contain Tex Mex staples such as nachos and quesadillas, the menu is well conceived and does homage to the original concept. We started off by splitting (thankfully because it was a huge portion) a special appetizer which was a salmon roulade. As I could tell, salmon was spread with goat cheese, seasoned , rolled, then battered and fried. It was served atop a curry/mustard cream sauce. It was outstanding in every way. My lovely dining companion ordered a chicken and portobello quesadilla, and I ordered seafood (shrimp and oyster) roll your own tacos served with guacamole, sour cream, lettuce tomato, and remoulade on the side. Both were very good choices. The space is nice too, very warm and inviting, lively without being out of control. The service was excellent and the prices were reasonable. Can't wait to go back.

text: Seriously, Tucson, start making the right restaurants popular (and start eating here more). You do have good food in town, but the mediocre joints are the ones you so often patronize. *OK, brush that chip off my shoulder* Sorry. And on with the review... I can't believe it took me so long to try Curry Leaf. I've eaten here twice now and the food has been excellent. Good samosas, good distinct curries, good naan. They have a whole section of dosas I haven't tried yet. The ingredients are treated with respect. The preparation is light and healthy, the way Indian food should be. Not the heavy, greasy preparations found at the NY style Indian places in town. It's hard to believe people have gotten bad naan here, but every restaurant sends out bad food sometimes, so I'll believe those reviewers. However, both naans I've gotten here were perfect. Crispy bits on the outside, fully-cooked but steamy and pliant on the inside. The garlic naan had a hint of fennel that made it beautifully balanced. That sense of spice, coupled with the lightness of the preparations makes me suspect ayurvedic techniques at play, but that's a bit more than I understand about Indian cuisine. That quality and level of thought in the food makes the smaller portions/higher prices thing well worth it; you actually feel good after eating here. That said, the gulab jamon was second, or even third rate. Hard and dense in an uninteresting syrup, but truth be told, I've only once in my life had this dessert at a restaurant and thought it was better than second rate. So getting that dish right is a bonus, not a necessity, in my book. Missing one star because of the dessert, and I'd like to see a few other dishes on the menu, but maybe I'm being unfair on both counts. This might go to five after a couple more meals.

Notes: * Don't eat the morning of (and night before?) the festival to max stomach space for yums. * Walk on sidewalks for free smells (kitchen vents out the back of the trucks) * Walk on sidewalks to fast track to desired destination(s) * Bring cash - don't let a faulty card swipey thing stand in the way of noms! * Bike/take mass transit if possible - vehicle parking is scarce! text: The infamous La Colombe, Frankford Ave...I want to give this barn like palace five stars but I just can't. Let's talk about the good stuff first... The artsy Fishtown location feels dominating and towering inside, like a large night club, but guess what? It works phenomenally for coffee and spirits! It's a breath of fresh air, compared to the average miniature coffee shop. After eating a chocolate chip muffin I decided to rob the place. I went to the counter and said, "Put all the pastries in my bag", "and put whatever doesn't fit, in your organic cardboard boxes". They stared. I frowned. Back to my seat. Yes, they are that good. I'm always impressed by the coffee selections, they live up to the unique descriptions. The fact that you can also get coffee been brewed beer adds a bit of fun and creativity to the menu. Feel free to skate around this palace and gauk at shiney espresso machines and beefy beer distillation machines... fancy-shmancy glam. You will find yourself surrounded by gigantic wooden doors, and bakers-a-bakin, I feel like I'm watching an Amish farm operate sometimes. It's very interesting. So far, so gooood... but then, disaster strikes.... LA COLOMBE HATES WHIPPED CREAM... They don't have this heavenly coffee balancing foam anywhere in the vaccinity. I thought to myself, are they a cult? What's going on!? I had to double check my surroundings, as I tripped over a little bit, I had to make sure I wasn't accidentally inducted in. I almost cried when I discovered this. I begged them for an alternative. Creme fresh? I don't know.. You can't mess with one of the best things to happen to my mouth since, ever. You might be the new coffee mob boss on the block, Godfather Colombe, but you can't mess with the Diety of the whipped! You're a whipped cream athiest. But I still accept you.. Ok, so I'll forgive you (cringing) for that. But should I get over the fact that your baristas seem like they are best friends Juno? I'm not the only one who feels like this btw. Every time I visit I feel like I'm being taken care of by a mr. or mrs. hipster neutrality. I noticed some batistas smile, but no one seems that cheerful. Maybe they need some whipped cream? But overall all the workers seem cool and smart! The waiters are the nicest of the bunch. The solution for more smiles= whipped cream. The seating looks great, and most of it is designed comfortably (even though you will only find solid wood for your tush..) but I miss a comfy couch or chair to study on. Comfort is half the reason I visit a coffee shop. It's still here. The rocking chair area is very comfy. Just no padding for the tush... The Amish nod. Did the owner grow up sleeping on a wooden bed? Honestly La Colombe is half in the 3 star zone, but makes up for it by going overboard into the 5 star zone, with great coffee and more. So that puts us at 4 stars. It's a mixed feeling kind of place, a fancy palace to take your out of town friends. It's already filled with touristy flockers. It's exciting but different. Thanks for the great coffee.
label: POS

I was surprised to see him raise his voice at a woman that looked like he could be his grandmother. It was awful! The cheeseteak: Nope. Nope. Nope. Bland, unappetizing. That's not authentic cheesesteakness! The mildly redeeming part of the meal were the fries, which would be pretty tough to screw up. I didn't particularly like the homeless people basically playing the role of busser and hoping that they would get some type of donation from a patron. I like to eat in peace, thank you very much. text: Forget the APPLE store, bring your damaged phone here. "It can't be fixed. You're screen is damaged and we can't replace it. You're going to have to get a new phone." These were the words that were told to my girlfriend when she brought her non-working iPhone 6 plus into the apple store this morning after we waited over an hour to see one of their technicians. Disappointed we discussed her options for a new phone, but the only thing she cared about was that she was going to loose all of the pictures she had that had not been backed up in months. We decided to take the phone head home and see if there was some way that we could get the pictures from her phone. When we got home we quickly realized that without being able to enter in her pass code we were out of luck. However, this is where Reno iPhone repair comes into play. As a last ditch effort we decided that we would take it into these guys and see if maybe they could help us out. Well, help us out they did. We walked right up to their booth, did not wait a single minute to be seen (remember at apple it took us over an hour to be seen and we were there 15 minutes before apple opened), told them the situation, (Or I did, all she could tell them was that she wanted her pictures) and immediately they offered us some ideas. The gentleman behind the counter said what he could do was hook up a new screen, see if it powers on, and if it did they could get in and help her get her photos backed up via iCloud, then they could put her old screen back in, and they would only charge us $35 for their time. Great we said, lets do it. They immediately pulled her phone apart right in front of us, hooked up a new screen, and low and behold, it powered right up. The gentleman then checked a few things, powered down her phone and put her OLD screen back in. He told us her screen looked ok and that he wanted to check it one more time. He pressed the power button and it powered back up without any issue and we NO new parts. He checked the function of the screen said everything looked good, and put the whole phone back together. We left there less than 15 minutes after we came in, with no new parts, and a 100% functioning phone that APPLE told us could not be repaired. I can not give this company enough praise for their customer service, their skill and their honesty. If you have an iPhone hardware problem don't waste your time at the APPLE store, bring it here instead and be assured that everything that could be done has been done.

text: 8 weeks after opening this is possibly the newest addition to the St Pete trend of repurposed service-stations-turned-eateries. Urban Comfort offers interesting, high-quality cocktails and their own take on southern-urban comfort food. Three years ago I would have swooned myself unconscious over this place. However after being exposed to places like casita taqueria, queens head, and the repurposed warehouse/shop atmospheres of Green Bench and 3 Daughters breweries this place feels like the "next" in a group of new-concept yet retro, qualitycentric establishments. Don't misunderstand me....Urban Comfort is a very nice place, and I feel they do fulfill their tagline's proclamation of "Simple Foods Done Exceptionally Well." We had the Comfort Burger and Fresh Catch Fried Fish. In a word the burger was "substantial." It had a home made quality, and a beautiful bun that could not stand up to the deliciously meaty burger and indulgent toppings. A second bun on the side would have been a nice lifesaver while eating this monster. The half order of fried fish and hushpuppies we also ordered was good...not great. The biscuit was a bit dry and a little tough, but so were my grandma's, so....nostalgic. The creamed-corn was very good. I also enjoyed the cucumber salad....hand cut cukes in a lightly sweet solution...definitely made on site. Once again --remembrances of grandma's table. The last thing I'll mention is the attentive and professional server. She rightfully prepared me for the flavor of star anise in the Gin Gypsy cocktail, which was refreshing in the summer heat. While I wasn't crazy about the drink it was not the fault of the cocktail...just not my favorite flavor profile. I look forward to trying more food and drink at my next visit.

text: I signed up about 5 months ago, and I finally got around to going to a dinner last night! It was at the Hyatt Regency in one of the ballrooms, so there was plenty of space to hang out and watch the food being made. There were two amuse bouche dishes before the main meal - a beet soup with a beet chip and goat cheese ravioli type thing, and a curry roasted carrot with whipped feta. I wasn't a huge fan of the soup, but the goat cheese part was fantastic. I also think the carrot could've been more cooked, but the flavors were very good. We ended up sitting next to a girl who knew my SO, and the others sitting by us were quite friendly and conversational, so we had some great company. The main meal started with some freshly baked onion rolls, which were nice and hot and tasty. Then we were served course by course with beer pairings from Bayou Teche: Course 1: Chef Matt Regan roasted duck breast & confit leg | braised red cabbage | turnip purée | Louisiana citrus & mustard jus | Acadie Beer Very good duck and puree, not a huge fan of the cabbage. Would've liked more puree. Course 2: Chef Tony Marinas Louisiana crab salad | smoked gulf prawns | tomato confit | avocado puree | Saison D'Ecrevisses Beer Really enjoyed the flavor of the smoked shrimp, but didn't feel it was cooked quite right. Crab salad was very good. Course 3: Chef Sylvain Tonello red snapper | Spanish chorizo crust | cannellini bean & ratatouille | pesto | Coteau Rodaire Beer Favorite course! The snapper was perfectly cooked and seasoned. The chorizo 'crust' was more of a chip, and was D-E-Licious! The ratatouille had good flavor, but wasn't out-of-this-world. Course 4: Chef Nilda de los Santos pan roasted venison & juniper berry | exotic mushroom confit | hackberry jus | truffle purée | Syrup in the Sky Beer My least favorite course. The venison was quite tough, but had good flavor. The berry's were ok, but kinda weird. I don't like mushrooms. The beer was very good. Course 5: Chef Milan Smith greek yogurt panna cotta | pistachio praline | chicory toffee | caramelized milk granita | Biere Noire Float with Madagascar Vanilla Bean Foam AWESOMENESS!!! The dessert was light, but amazingly flavorful. Every item was perfectly done and complimented all the other items. And the beer float was perfect to go with it. It was a very good experience overall. The price for the meal and ambience and everything is about right, and it is all you can drink. So you can get your money's worth pretty easily (we enjoyed some Tempranillo wine in addition to the pairings). I also like that they give you comment/critique cards at the beginning, so you can fill it in as you eat. It made me feel like a real food judge! I'd highly recommend dinner lab to anyone interested in a unique dining experience.
label: POS

text: Absolutely horrid. Worst childcare mistake my husband and I have ever made in 3.5 years. Aside from a handful of staff who are genuinely excellent with children and seem to have real childcare experience, the rest are absolutely clueless about how to care for a child. The worst of all is Lee, the director, who I never once saw interact with any of the children, yet he felt it appropriate to lecture my husband and I daily about our parenting. Completely out of line and unprofessional. Though the facility claims to focus on the individual development and needs of each child there, in reality the children are grouped up and constantly shuffled around between different teachers and if a child doesn't fit into their "system", such as if a child doesn't nap for example, they are completely unprepared to accommodate that child's needs and instead choose to punish that child as if they were misbehaving. Takes a very conformist approach to childcare. A good child with a unique or spirited personality will have a very difficult time there if they don't conform to the formula. The "curriculum" is less focused on actual learning of useful skills and information and instead on teaching children about subjects they don't really need to be learning at their age. Is it nice that they told my daughter what "astronaut" is in Spanish? Sure. Did she really need to know it given that they don't actually teach Spanish in a way that children can truly learn it? No, I think not. If you're going to teach something, then teach it properly so that the student learns it not just memorized and regurgitates it on command like a parrot. That's not education, that's training. The facility itself is a series of closed isolating rooms and is always cold, no matter what the time of year or temperature. The daily activity reports are all pre-printed at the beginning of the day and generic. Nebulous scale for judging a child's behavior. Parents expected to correct bad behavior with almost no contextual information about it beyond generic footnotes such as "was disruptive in class" "not listening" and "yelling". Lee will swear up and down that he can accommodate any schedule since the facility is open 6am to 6:30pm, but in reality he DEMANDS that children (at least the preschoolers) be there no later than 9am every morning or they will be turned away. Likewise if a parent is even a little late picking up a child the facility will call child services and turn the child over to them. (Not hyperbole, actually stated in TLE rulebook.) They are heinously overpriced considering they can't even manage to wipe a child's nose or give the child a tissue to do it themselves. From feeding children the standard Sodexo fare of hamburgers and chicken nuggets for lunch everyday to the sad little cubby next the front desk with a filthy little mat on the floor they call an "infirmary", I could go on and on, however the very worst thing about this place was that my daughter who loves to learn and has been in daycare since she was 6 months old, HATED going there. She would literally cry and scream and beg us not to take her there EVERY. SINGLE. DAY. for 5 months until today when we finally had enough and said good bye to that place forever. I cannot stress enough that if you value your child's individual emotional and mental development then do not waste your time or money at The Learning Experience.

text: Having bought three cars at the Jeep store over the years, went back for a fourth. We agreed on a deal that included moving my winch from the old jeep to the new jeep. The salesman took both Jeeps over to a service guy named Ashton who said it could be done without any parts and it would take 4-5 hours. So we signed papers to buy the new jeep. The paperwork in writing stated they would move the winch over as part of the deal. We took the Wrangler the next day back to have the work done. For those reading this--each bumper has a unique bolt pattern as does each winch--so usually need a winch plate that goes between the winch and the bumper. We were told they could use our winch plate. After we dropped our Jeep off go get the work done 9 AM, we received a call that they would need to make a plate--ok no worries. Then an hour later, got a call that the labor was 12-13 hours that they would eat, but it would cost me 478.00 for the plate--said what? That was in the paperwork--said if I didn't pay it--they were going to unwind the deal. Told them fine--unwind the deal. I said--and if you read these reviews, the worst department is Service at that store--why if service quoted sales 4-5 hours and no parts wouldn't service have to go with what they said? Anyway--we left the conversation that night with the SM going to talk to the GM--but looked like because instead of 500 bucks it was going to be 2k--they were going to unwind the deal. The quote was "friends are friends, but business is business." So I called my friends at Chapman Jeep in Scottsdale--they were willing to match the deal--made it better by 800 bucks (jeep sticker was 600 more and their deal was 200 less) and were willing to move the winch and get the right plate. They were willing to come get my Jeep from Phoenix and bring me my new Jeep--hmm ok. The next morning, the GM, Ted called--said he'd now eat the cost of the plate. I said Ted--I'm a bit like a yo-yo here--first its on--then its off--now its back on--asked if he would unwind the deal--said he would and I could pick up my old jeep. Went at the end of the day to pick up my Jeep--I had to move my taillight cages back over--get all my stuff out and and they lost one of my keys. The sales man, Sam, came over and watched me work--and they sent a customer service manager, Ken, who actually made me feel ok with my decision--his best quote--"for smart guys, these guys can be pretty dumb." You would think there would be more discussion--I did say if they wanted to do Chapman's deal, I'd keep the Jeep but they passed. Sam the salesman did warn me that I needed to be careful because if I went to Phoenix, more than likely I'd be ripped off--lol really? So--off I drove. That night I got a congratulations email from Jeep and a survey--well, right, they didn't do very well. Over the weekend and into the next week, I received a voicemail from Ted the GM asking me to call him--it was important. He was upset because I gave him a bad survey. Then later in the day, I received a phone call from the salesman, Sam, wanting to grind on me because he lost the sale and got hurt on the survey. When I ended the phone call--he started texting me. These folks are stalkers!! The issue for me is plain and simple--do what you committed to do. The phone call with the we're going to unwind the deal if you don't pay is not good business. Craziest news of the day? The sales manager elected to end our business relationship saying he had ethics--wow, really? Now the rest of the story, worked with Scottsdale Chapman Jeep, they picked up my Jeep, did paperwork at my office, left me a loaner car, and brought my brand new Jeep to Tucson detailed with a full tank of gas. Now that I think about it--good thing Phoenix came to me, I was so worried Sam would be right and I'd be ripped off if I bought a car phoenix--NOT. text: This is a charming little coffee shop in the middle of downtown Audubon. I think charming is the best word to describe this place. They're happy to accommodate if you want to modify something on the menu. Sometimes I come here just for coffee, and sometimes I order food. The coffee is good, and they have plenty of tea options if you don't like coffee. I recently ordered the chicken salad for lunch. It was tasty and filling. Treehouse has plenty of healthy options plus vegetarian and vegan options if you don't eat animal products. I try to eat relatively healthy when I go out, so this place gets an A for healthy options. (If you're not into health food, don't worry. There's plenty here for you, too.) The noise levels here are always reasonable. They play music, but it's not too loud. Sure, the restaurant offers a fun atmosphere with plenty of seating both inside and out; it has a scenic view of the Delaware Canal; and it's located in the fun area of Lambertville. It's BYOB and has a diverse selection of menu items from veggies, salads, soups, oysters, steaks, seafood and more. Unfortunately, the service we experienced was horrendous. We arrived promptly for our 7:30 reservation and were seated right away, but weren't greeted by a server for a good ten minutes. Once we were greeted, it took another 30+ minutes to place our food order, and then we waited more than an hour and fifteen minutes before our entrees arrived. That being said, we did have oysters (a couple of different kinds) that were awesome. We attempted to order a salad but were told they were out of the salad we wanted.... bummer. We also shared a side of cauliflower pure, a side of asparagus, and the scallop entree. All were OK - nothing to write home about. We would have liked to wash dinner down with water in addition to our wine, but we had to ask several times before getting that... The manager was more apologetic to us than our waiter was, and the table next to us made a point to lean over to share their disappointment with the service as well. I recommend that if you do head to Hamilton's, to do so on a weeknight... unless you don't mind a very long and leisurely meal.

text: Went here for a birthday lunch with my other half. .We're Los Angeles transplants, a city that host some of the best Asian cuisine in the country, not to mention we're both foodies. We've found since arriving here a year ago that authentic Asian foods have not found their way to the first state and that what is available in this category is sadly lacking. Takumi is a perfect example. They market themselves as "authentic Japanese, but serve a fusion of Asian food styles. Today, we both ordered the #1 Bento Box which comes with teriyaki chicken, shrimp/vegi tempura, salad, white rice, and chef's choice sashimi... I never got to the sashimi. I was put off before even getting to it. The teriyaki chicken tasted strange...almost like turkey..and the sauce was bland. It carried no taste at all and certainly would not be identified as anything resembling teriyaki in a blind taste test. Teriyaki should either be slightly sweet or even spicy, either way it should be flavorful enough to taste. Turning to the tempura for solace I was again disappointed when met with a droopy, soggily coated shrimp without an ounce of taste! It seemed quite amazing to me that a chef could remove "taste" from not one, but 2 food sources. The salad ...everyday iceberg lettuce...I would later find out, swims in bottled Benihana salad dressing. The dressing had taste at least! Feeling like I simply did not want to partake in a meal that I wasn't enjoying and it is my birthday, I explained to the waitress that I was dissatisfied with the quality of the meal, I ask if she would please trade it in for a simple California Roll. Well, apparently removing taste is a habit of Takumi's owner as I was tastelessly told "no" that I could not do that. I was offered to replace the teriyaki chicken with some Chinese dish which I did not ask for, nor want. At this point I am wondering who runs this place...he/she who cares so little about customer service. I ask the waitress to please send the manager out. I gentleman approached the table to inform us that the manager was not there and that I could "talk to me". I ask "and who is me? What is your position here?" Astoundingly, this man replied "the owner". Really? And this is how you present yourself? I should not be surprised since he clearly has little concern for his foods presentation either. I explain my side and ask why I cannot get the California Roll iu ask for in lieu of the meal I dislke. I'm told by the supposed owner of Takumi that no one else today has complained. Please note that there is one..yes one...other party of 3 in the restaurant. So, basically I've been told that my opinion is invalid..but, of course my money is not. There followed more banter without once even a glimpse of an explanation as to why giving me what I want was not an option. Did I need to pay a difference? Did I need to know an ancient Japanese code? Nope, just pissed the owner off that I questioned the quality of the food. When i ask if the tempura was frozen he would not confirm or deny. My other half ask if he tasted the food from his kitchen. "sometimes" was the owners answer. Sometimes??? Really??? If you don't know what your food taste like then don't serve it and certainly don't reprimand someone who tells you that the taste is a problem. I have no idea what kind of business Takumi does, but I believe that anyone who is familiar with authentic Asian cuisine will not find Takumi satisfying.

text: We did a sea kayak tour on Santa Cruz island. We got the boat from Ventura. It's quite easy to find and plenty of parking. Arrive a little early so that you can complete forms. There are other kayak tours and campers and day hikers leaving from this spot so you have to find the right check in person. But that is no problem at all. The boat ride over is about an hour. If u get sea sick take some Dramamine before hand. There are snacks and drinks to buy on the boat. Once you arrive you head to the kayaks where they will go through a safety and education piece. Don't worry if you've never kayaked before there are all levels here. You can store your stuff in a big container while you kayak. Bring some water and maybe a snack for the kayak tour. Depending on the temp u may feel cold and they have jackets and bottoms u can borrow and wear as u will get very wet and inside the caves can be chilly. We did not feel we needed them and it was overcast when we were there. You'll kayak for a couple of hours. It's tiring! Be aware of this :) but so much fun. The caves are incredible and the guides are knowledgeable fun and safe. They will help you if you need it. One of our party got exhausted and one of the guides just towed them. When you get back you can then hike or snorkel. They provide wet suits and all the gear. There is nothing on the island, so bring food and water with you and a change of clothing, again if the temps are low u will want to have something warm to put on. I really enjoyed this trip it was probably one of the best kayak tours I've done.

text: I recently took my 1974 Mercedes Roadster to Rex Carle Automotive for some engine, brake system and electrical work. In searching for the "right guy" to do the work on my car, I asked around and all signs pointed to Rex -- including that he is a Bosch Authorized Repair Center which is a critically important detail, especially when servicing Mercedes engine & fuel systems. Immediately upon meeting Rex during an initial inspection of the car, it was blatantly evident that he is the real deal. Very knowledgeable, detail oriented, and genuine. I felt instantly comfortable with his ability to do the right job and take care of my classic Mercedes. After working up a list of parts include an entire rebuild of the fuel injection hose system (no small feat when done properly); check valves, replacing all brake lines, rebuilding brake reservoir, belts, oil, ps cleanup, fix a misfire, adjust surging idle, inspection and fix turn signal, we set a date to drop the car. Dropped the car on a Monday morning and told him to take whatever time was needed. Picked the car up on Thursday morning. WOW would be an understatement. The moment I started the car, you could tell it was running "as delivered" from the dealership. This car had been in our family since 1979 and I hadn't heard it sound like this since the 80's. Idle, perfect. Not a drop of movement or shake on the tachometer. Smooth and silky. Took the car out and up the hill -- the tires actually spun! (not that i'm doing that in my 74 -- but it happened). On the highway home, I was smiling at how well the car worked again. Plus, Rex fixed my turn signal switch. These parts are NLA and he just took it apart and fixed it. I can't express enough how professional, honest, genuine and great an experience it is to work with Rex and his team. Cost? How much is it worth to have the right job done to your favorite car... But seriously, very competitive and I haven't thought about the cost after feeling the result. Take your favorite Mercedes to Rex is my advice.

text: I met a group of friends here for dinner, and decided to make the reservation online to get the points. Since we were more than 6, I had to call. It took awhile (I'm attributing that to the fact that it was around New Year's), I spoke with a very personable gentleman who explained that they preferred to personally accomodate larger parties in case there were any special requests, etc. Score one for good communication. We were there on a Friday night, and aside from a large municipal lot adjacent to the restaurant that fills quickly, be forwarned that finding parking in Ambler is a challenge. Once I got to the restaurant, a few friends were already there and seated--with drinks. Our server was excellent. She was attentive without being overbearing, and was very knowledgeable about the menu. We started off with a cheeseboard, which is a great way to start the meal. Great spreads, mustards, chutneys and the cheeses were all amazing. It gave us ample time to peruse the rest of the menu. Lots of great, creative salads, and much variety across the board. I had an endive salad with roasted pumpkin in a bacon vinagrette for a starter. I enjoyed it, but wish they could have been a bit more generous with the vinaigrette--it was so good. That was the only downside of my meal. Pastas can be ordered in half portions--I had the pasta ribbons with roasted duck leg--it was delicious and so flavorful. Most of my friends had fish--either sea bass or dorade--and proclaimed their meals as very good. There are also a number of vegetarian selections on the menu as well. Drinks were large and well made--try the blackberry lemonade and the orange blossom martini. There is also a nice wine list as well as a large selection of craft beers. We weren't going to order desert--but when the menu came out, we couldn't resist. Pumpkin donuts--OMG! served with a scoop of hazelnut gelato--large enough to share. And we also had a very decadent dark chocolate desert that was incredibly rich and wonderful. As I mentioned--the service was very good, and they were nice enough to let us hang till after closing. It's pricey, but well worth it. Highly recommended.
